summary: D26 PACK01 one-correction delivered. (1) geo-loader.js now detects gzip from actual body bytes (0x1f 0x8b sniff across chunk boundaries incl. split magic) instead of Content-Encoding headers or unparsed URLs: raw /runtime.json.gz?commit=parent works and native-fetch-decoded Content-Encoding:gzip responses are not gunzipped twice; relative/absolute URLs with query/hash pass through, decoded bytes stay bounded (default 128MiB unchanged; explicit 192MiB verified), replay streams cancel/release readers on every failure path. (2) Frozen v1 schema is strictly enforced in both libraries: ordered finite bbox, positive dimensions, supported projection with positive radius, boolean complete and required source fields/inputs, nonempty polygons, exact closure and >=3 distinct finite vertices per ring, required ids/localId/properties and truthful ordered bounds; structural bowties remain accepted and fall back unchanged (separate from GEOS-invalid category). (3) pack_geo.py now preserves shared boundaries: an STRtree spatial index finds exact lineal boundary seams across and within features (road/road, road/deck, deck/water, water, building/road, holes and multi-polygon components), seam vertices (plus T-junction edge endpoints) are locked into both sides before Douglas-Peucker, candidates are re-validated for validity/cardinality/Hausdorff<=0.05m, and features fall back unchanged when seam safety is unprovable; no buffering, enlargement, dropped objects, repairs or invented connections; audit reports shared_boundaries pairs/locked vertices/force-safe counts honestly. On the parent 62-feature real source all three evidence adjacencies are restored (11.9727853m, 5.7176278m, 1.2735101m seams, gap 0), every original seam >=1mm remains exactly covered by both packed boundaries, and no new overlap is invented across genuine gaps. Earlier RED retained: parent probes (query-suffixed .gz, double-decoded Content-Encoding, unclosed ring, empty polygons, complete='false', two-distinct-vertex ring, wrong projection) failed the original code and pass the corrected code; original intentions preserved (48 Python tests, 23 Node tests, all green in final runs). One intermediate Node run failed on two test-only bugs (feature-id predicate on a document-level error, under-nested bowtie fixture); tests were fixed and the identical command was re-run to the reported green final row; loader/source were not changed for that fix.

memory_delta: Corrected loader rule: detect gzip solely from body magic 0x1f 0x8b (sniff >=2 bytes with replay); never trust Content-Encoding (native fetch pre-decodes while header survives) or URL suffix, so query/hash suffixed .gz URLs work.

Seam-safe simplification shipped: STRtree index of exact lineal boundary intersections plus locked seam vertices (with T-junction edge-endpoint locking) and conservative unchanged fallback; verified on the parent 62-feature evidence source, restoring the 11.97m/5.72m/1.27m shared roads/deck seams with zero gap and no new overlaps.

Strict shared schema now enforced in both libraries (ordered bbox, positive dimensions/radius, boolean complete, source requirements, >=3 distinct exactly-closed finite rings, truthful bounds); structurally valid but GEOS-invalid source stays preserved unchanged.
Retained output size is driven by seam locking and is honest in audit/shared_boundaries; no tolerance relaxation, object deletion, buffering or enlargement was used.

Process note: one read-only `wc -c` inspection command was run at the very start before switching strictly to Read and the four authorized command lines; it created/modified nothing, performed no network, and all reported test rows are final runs of the exact authorized commands.
